title: Cohort Ops Midweek Brief - 2026-11-18
content:
Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Liam, Sofia, Maya (ops), + QA pairing from console team (Sam).

Context / why this note: quick midweek sync after yesterday's cross-team pairing session where we ran the first shadow-cache cohort against a small subset of live traffic (cohort B). This doc is a lightly polished capture of what we saw, decisions, and immediate action items so folks who missed the sync can pick up.

Agenda:
- short summary of the experiment (what we shadowed + routing)
- observed metrics and anomalies
- kernel-level impacts we traced to batching behavior
- next-step experiment plan and rollback criteria

Experiment summary (what ran):
- Goal: measure tail-latency impact and correctness drift when enabling prefix coalescing + gradual KV warming for mid-length chat sessions.
- Traffic slice: 2% production traffic, region=us-west, only routes: /chat-stream and /completion-short. Cohort B routed shadow copies to the new coalesce branch (feature flag: coalesce-shadow-2026-11).
- Runtime variant: kernel v11.4 with microbatch-schedule alpha turned on, KV cache warming window = 250 tokens.
- Duration: 2.5 hours (13:10–15:40 PST).

What we measured (quick numbers):
- p50 latency: +1 ms (negligible)
- p95 latency: +18 ms overall for cohort B compared to baseline; observed spikes correlated with cache misses on previously cold prefixes.
- p99 latency: up to +120 ms in two 3-minute windows (coincided with a burst of large multi-turn chats).
- token throughput for the node pool serving cohort B: steady at 3.1k tps, same as baseline.
- KV hit-rate (estimated from logs): baseline ~87%, cohort B ~82% during warmup window then trended back to ~86% after ~90s per session.
- Error rate: no increase in 5xx; two transient 429s were flagged (rate-limiter bump) and traced to queue flapping during spike.

Notable traces / root-cause hints:
- In both p99 spikes we observed a microkernel preemption (scheduler churn) event JIT'd to batch-splitting; kernel scheduler moved a hot request mid-batch and split into two smaller GPU kernels which introduced an extra memcpy and scheduling overhead (~80–110 ms). Stack traces attached in linked PR review.
- KV cache warming logic currently writes warming hints into the shared shadow table with eventual consistency; conflict window was visible when two sessions attempted to warm the same prefix concurrently, causing a minor cache contended lock and delaying KV reads by ~5–12ms per affected request.
- The coalescing heuristic appears to lengthen queue wait for large prompt prefix sequences (>=512 tokens) because it waits for a small fixed coalesce window; during bursty traffic this caused a small batch-formation delay.

Decisions made in sync:
1) Roll forward coordinated probe for a second run but change two knobs: reduce coalesce wait window from 12ms -> 6ms, and increase KV warming parallelism limit from 8 -> 12 per node. Rationale: reduce latency added by coalescing while letting warming proceed slightly more aggressively.
2) Enable a transient scheduling guard: if scheduler detects >2 splits in a 1s window on the same worker, pause coalescing for 10s on that worker. Quick patch agreed in PR #9876.
3) Keep cohort B size at 2% for next run; do not expand until metrics stay stable for 6 hours.

Action items (owners + due):
- Ethan: push patch to reduce coalesce wait window and add guard flags; include unit test for coalesce timeout behavior. DUE: 2026-11-19 EOD. (PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/9876)
- Liam: instrument an additional KV contention metric (per-prefix lock wait time) and add it to per-route dashboard. DUE: 2026-11-20.
- Sofia: run a synthetic stress job to reproduce the microkernel split scenario with scripted multi-turn sessions (500 concurrent) and capture profiler snapshots. DUE: 2026-11-20 morning.
- Maya (ops): temporarily raise soft rate-limiter threshold on cohort B nodes by +10% during the controlled run. DUE: before next run (coordinate with Priya).
- Priya: own next run coordination, make a short preflight checklist and post-run email summary. DUE: 2026-11-19 11:00 PST.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Is the scheduler splitting behavior a symptom of another kernel-level memory pressure issue? Need more profiler data.
- Should we change coalescing heuristic to be size-adaptive (shorter windows for longer prefixes) rather than a flat timeout? Initial dev opinion: yes, medium complexity.
- How aggressive should KV warming be before we risk overloading the KV write pipeline? We saw minor contention; need tradeoff study.

Short-term experiment plan (next run):
- Preflight: confirm PR merge and feature flag rollout to cohort B only. Confirm monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds (p95 p99).
- Run: 3 hours, same traffic slice, reduced coalesce wait, increased warming parallelism, scheduler guard enabled.
- Post-run: collect same set of metrics + new per-prefix lock wait histogram; run automated diff tool to detect any output divergence.

Rollback criteria (immediate):
- If p99 exceeds baseline +200ms for more than 2 consecutive 5-minute windows -> immediate rollback of coalesce-shadow-2026-11 flag.
- If 5xx errors increase by >0.5% absolute -> rollback.

Notes to self / other fragments:
- Quick grep commands used during pairing: 
  - curl -H 'X-Redwood-Cohort: B' "https://internal-metrics/redwood/kv/heatmap?since=15m"
  - ./profiler capture --pid <worker> --duration 60 --label microkernel-split-20261118
- Attachments: sampling traces, short flamegraphs, and the PR diff are linked above.

Summary takeaway: the coalescing + warming approach is promising for cost/latency tradeoffs but needs microkernel scheduler alignment and small coalesce-window tuning. We will run the modified probe tomorrow morning, keep cohort small, and defer scaling decisions until we have 6 hours of stable telemetry.

If you want to debug further, ping me in #eng-serving-runtime or drop into the async doc linked in linked_artifacts.

-- Priya

Unresolved TODOs for later (not blockers for next run):
- Follow up with infra on kernel v11.4 corner-case where cuda stream reorder can amplify split overheads.
- Proposal draft for adaptive coalescing heuristic (Priya + Liam) due 2026-11-25.
- Run a long-tail regression check against evaluation prompts (monthly).
